info.title: Spacefast API
info.description:
API for sharing AI artifacts, managing spaces, claiming anonymous publishes, and operating versions.

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/v1`). Operations marked `deprecated` also send RFC 9745 `Deprecation` and RFC 8594 `Sunset` headers, plus a `Link` with `rel="deprecation"` pointing at the versioning and deprecation policy: https://spacefast.com/docs/api/versioning

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 with explicit Spacefast capability scopes. Use the authorization-code flow for people and client credentials for machines.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required for the browser approval flow. Optional for a credential that has `tokens:create`. Use a client-generated key of at most 255 characters. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

parameters.name: X-Spacefast-Continuation-Token
parameters.description: Continuation token from an approved `confirmation_required` response. Send it only with the same request body and Idempotency-Key.

get.summary: Read the context of your token
get.description: Introspects the caller behind the request. Any caller can read it — a browser session, an API key, a machine credential, a Space key, a partner token, or no credential at all — and every answer carries the Spacefast agent instructions as Markdown, filtered by `scopes` and budgeted for the `consumer`. An authenticated caller also gets a `credential` block naming what kind of token it is and what it is bound to, and a user-owned interactive grant gets a `capabilities` map of the operations its scopes allow.

schema.description: Comma-separated (or repeated) AGENT_PROSE fragment keys.
Which client is reading, so the fragments come back shaped for it.

$schema.description: Canonical JSON Schema URL for this response body. The server also sends it in the `Link: rel="describedby"` response header.

consumer.description: Which client is reading, so the fragments come back shaped for it.

scopes.description: The instruction fragment keys included in `markdown`, in reading order.

markdown.description: The Spacefast agent instructions. Identical for every caller.

credential.description: The credential behind this request and what it is bound to. Absent for an anonymous caller.

kind.description: What the caller presented, in the platform's own credential vocabulary.

post.summary: Publish files and get a live URL
post.description: Publishes already-built files directly, or turns a zip/tar project archive into a durable Spacefast CI build that runs the Spacefast CLI. A zip that is already a website publishes immediately, exactly like a file manifest; an archive that needs a build, such as Next.js, goes to CI and its receipt returns `next.action=poll`, staying available at that status link until the Build settles. On a Spacefast-managed Space, buildable source is first committed to the Space's hosted repository and the Build runs from that commit — the receipt's `git` block carries the remote and the Build's `input.commit` names the sha, so later `git push`es to the same remote continue the same history. Direct publishes wait for the finalize to complete by default; pass `async=1` to return immediately with an operation link to poll. The two user-facing links are Open (reusable access) and, for anonymous Spaces, Claim (one-time ownership transfer). New Spaces are Private by default. Pass `spaceId` to update an existing Space; otherwise a new Space is created.

parameters.name: async
parameters.description: Controls the finalize transport. Omit the parameter, or pass `0` or `false`, to wait for the finalize and return the terminal receipt, degrading to a poll receipt only at the in-request ceiling. Pass `1` or `true` to return immediately with the operation to poll. Project archives always return a durable Build receipt and poll URL instead of holding the request open.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A credential-free publish request that sends this header must also send X-Spacefast-Idempotency-Principal. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

parameters.name: X-Spacefast-Idempotency-Principal
parameters.description: Required with Idempotency-Key on a credential-free publish. Send a stable 64-character hexadecimal value that only the caller knows, and send it unchanged on every retry. It isolates the stored one-time claim and upload credentials from other anonymous callers. Never log or share this value.

repository.description: `owner/name` of the GitHub repository this space deploys from, else null.

defaultBranch.description: Branch that publishes to the live channel when pushed.

provisioned.description: Whether the repository behind this block exists yet. Always true for a GitHub binding; for a hosted remote, true once it was minted or first pushed to, and false while there is nothing to browse.

git.description: Git remote for this space, or null when it has no repository yet. Push to `remoteUrl` to publish.

fix.description: Concrete, agent-actionable remediation hint, when one can be derived.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same operation can resolve this diagnostic without the caller changing anything.

key.description: The space key (sfc_…): the one credential for this unclaimed space. Bearer auth for publish, update, status, sharing, rotation, and the one-time continuation exchange. Returned only at creation and rotation; save it immediately.

url.description: The site door: the live URL with the space key in /__/<key> form. Opening it exchanges the key for a private view session and lands on the site. It is the same key in URL form, so share it as carefully as the key.

claimUrl.description: Claim page link in /claim#<key> form. The fragment is the key; browsers never send it to a server and the claim page strips it before analytics. Works until expiresAt and can be opened more than once.

default.description: Problem details (RFC 9457). Any 4xx/5xx response is one `application/problem+json` document.

get.description: Returns one space with its status, URLs, channels, and policy. Claim-token reads extend an anonymous space's expiry window.

post.summary: Create a build from a source archive, repository, or managed source
post.description: Creates a build that produces a version on success through the normal publish path. Repository inputs use the saved connection; source archive inputs receive an upload instruction the new build owns. Naming a managed `source` instead builds it from its connected production repository with the saved settings and live target. The caller cannot select source code, commands, settings, refs, or publish targets, and must send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a managed-source trigger without one fails with 422 `idempotency_key_required`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

parameters.description: Optional client-generated key, at most 255 characters, that makes this write safe to retry. The first request with a given key stores its outcome, scoped to your tenant, credential, and route. A retry with the same key and an identical body does not execute again: the server replays the stored response and marks it `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A request that reuses a key with a different body fails with 409 `idempotency_key_reused`. A duplicate request that arrives while the first is still in flight fails with 409 `idempotency_conflict_in_progress`. The server keeps each key for 24 hours.

post.summary: Run a WP-CLI command against a space
post.description: Runs one `wp` command against the space's own WordPress and waits for it to finish. This is the escape hatch beneath the named surfaces: anything WP-CLI can do that Spacefast has not given its own route. `args` is an already-split argument vector (`["option", "get", "blogname"]`), relayed verbatim — no shell parses it, so nothing re-splits or re-globs what you send. Requires write access to the space, because a `wp` command has unrestricted authority over the site's data, and every run is written to the space's activity trail. Note that the provider runs this as a job and reports only whether WP-CLI exited zero: `output` is null because WP Cloud exposes no channel carrying the command's own stdout.

dataSources.description: Named public WordPress sources exposed to repository builds; at most 32 entries.

propertyNames.description: Stable source identifier: 1-128 letters, numbers, or underscores; starts with a letter or underscore; excludes __proto__, constructor, and prototype.

url.description: Canonical public WordPress URL: lowercase https:// scheme; IDNA-normalized DNS labels (1-63 characters each, 253 total, alphanumeric edges, alphanumeric or hyphen interior), canonical dotted-decimal IPv4, or bracketed hexadecimal IPv6; optional nonzero port and UTF-8 path. Percent escapes are validated and canonicalized; encoded percent signs, slashes, backslashes, controls, invalid UTF-8, whitespace other than encoded ASCII path spaces, credentials, queries, fragments, and trailing-dot hosts are rejected. Default port, host case, IDNs, dot segments, path encoding, and trailing path slashes are normalized before storage.

additionalProperties.description: A public WordPress site exposed to repository builds as a content source.

defaultDataSource.description: Name of the configured source exposed through `WORDPRESS_URL`. It must match a `dataSources` entry. When omitted, the first source in bytewise name order is used.

config.description: Stored SpaceConfig overlay applied over the live version's sf.jsonc; null when nothing is overridden.

settingsDigest.description: CAS token for versioned settings writes (digest over title + config overlay). Send it back as baseSettingsDigest on PATCH to get compare-and-swap semantics.

noindex.description: When true, the live production hostnames serve platform noindex directives. Immutable version and preview hostnames are always noindex regardless of this setting.

pinnedAt.description: Instant the space was pinned to the top of its team's space list, or null when it is not pinned. The pin is team-wide: everyone who can see the team sees it.

managedBy.description: Who owns this space's git history. `spacefast`: push `remoteUrl` to publish. `github`: the space deploys from `repository` and direct pushes are refused.

remoteUrl.description: Credential-free git remote to push to, or null when `managedBy` is `github`. Authenticate as HTTP Basic user `t` with a space key or API key as the password.

repository.description: `owner/name` of the GitHub repository this space deploys from, else null.

defaultBranch.description: Branch that publishes to the live channel when pushed.

provisioned.description: Whether the repository behind this block exists yet. Always true for a GitHub binding; for a hosted remote, true once it was minted or first pushed to, and false while there is nothing to browse.

git.description: Git remote for this space, or null when it has no repository yet. Push to `remoteUrl` to publish.
